newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai bank employees end protest after demands met.
newsitem.headline: Thai bank employees end protest after demands met.

text.p: About 2,000 employees from the state-owned Krung Thai Bank Plc ended their protest for bigger year-end bonuses outside their Bangkok headquarters on Wednesday after their demands were met.

The protest came a day after employees from another Thai firm, Sanyo Universal Electric, burnt down a company warehouse and office building following their management's refusal to pay higher year-end bonuses.

Deputy Interior Minister Chalerm Yoobumroong told reporters after a meeting with top executives of the bank that the employees demands for a total bonus payment of 5-1/2 months for the year would be met.
Protesters said they were satisfied by the announcement and dispersed.
"The dispute has ended. Employees will get the 5-1/2 months of bonus. We will send the proposal to the cabinet for approval," the minister said.
Earlier, union officials had been offered 5.04 months in total year-end bonuses. The government would shoulder the burden of extra payments, Chalerm said.
Management and staff had been at odds on Wednesday over the size of the bonus payment. Negotiations between management and staff had broken down earlier.
Krung Thai Bank is majority-owned by the finance ministry and a Bank of Thailand fund.
Some of the protesters had vowed to continue protests through the night until demand were met, while others said threatened to go on strike on Thursday.
Police were hunting a group of about 20 employees from Sanyo Universal Electric suspected of starting Tuesday's blaze.
Thai premier Chavalit Yongchaiyudh said on Wednesday that the action taken by Sanyo employees could scare away foreign investors.
